evidence: Ter. Eun. 4.2.6: male sē habēre, to feel ill, dejected (Lewis & Short s.v. malus)
Cic. Att. 4.14.1: minus valēre … melius valēre (Lewis & Short s.v. valeō)

terms.gloss: lousy (as an answer to how are you?)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short gives īnfēlīciter only as “unhappily, unfortunately”, of things that turn out badly (fit mihi obviam īnfēlīciter, Ter. Eun. 2.3.36), never of health. Say Mē male habeō or Minus valeō.

phrases.english: What’s wrong? Where does it hurt?

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): pp. 55, 98.
